- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially >0.7), suggesting a lag in adjusting to bullish sentiment.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 70→76), model fails to correct downward quickly, showing overshoot bias and delayed mean reversion.
- When sentiment is low (e.g., <0.3), model underestimates true price drops, indicating underweighting of bearish signals.
- Forecast trend is often too smooth; fails to capture volatility clustering, especially in 30-day horizon where true outcomes show sudden jumps and corrections.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in early forecast days (e.g., 1st–3rd day of 30d forecast) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish — should adjust downward if sentiment is weak or declining.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2), model should reduce forecast slope and add downward buffer.
- Forecast should be capped at 10–15% above recent high if sentiment is bullish but volatile — to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
